candidates.source_name: Ephrem the Syrian / Commentary on Deuteronomy
candidates.source_attribution: Ephrem the Syrian, Commentary on Deuteronomy, on 33:8-11. NPNF Series 2, vol. 13. PD. Cf. Mt 10:37.
candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Deuteronomy (c. 365 AD)

On Moses' blessing of Levi — 'Who said unto his father and to his mother, I have not seen him; neither did he acknowledge his brethren, nor knew his own children: for they have observed thy word, and kept thy covenant' (Deu 33:9) — Ephrem reads the praise of Levi's denial-of-kin-for-sake-of-God as the canonical Old-Testament anchor of the dominical 'He that loveth father or mother more than me is not worthy of me' (Mt 10:37) and the Levitical-monastic ideal of leaving-family-for-God. Tewahedo monastic theology cites Deu 33:9 + Mt 10:37 as the canonical doubled-witness for the bahǝtawi's renunciation of family ties — the desert father is a Levite in the pattern of Deu 33:9, whose covenant-keeping is honoured precisely because it preferred God to kin.

candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Deuteronomy (c. 365 AD)

On Moses' blessing of Levi — 'Who said unto his father and to his mother, I have not seen him; neither did he acknowledge his brethren, nor knew his own children: for they have observed thy word, and kept thy covenant' (Deu 33:9) — Ephrem reads the praise of Levi's denial-of-kin-for-sake-of-God as the canonical Old-Testament anchor of the dominical 'He that loveth father or mother more than me is not worthy of me' (Mt 10:37) and the Levitical-monastic ideal of leaving-family-for-God. Tewahedo monastic theology cites Deu 33:9 + Mt 10:37 as the canonical doubled-witness for the bahǝtawi's renunciation of family ties — the desert father is a Levite in the pattern of Deu 33:9, whose covenant-keeping is honoured precisely because it preferred God to kin.
